title: React effects refs imperative handles and external systems
concepts: Effects synchronize a committed React component with an external system; they are not a general mechanism for deriving one piece of React state from another.
An Effect has setup, optional cleanup, and reactive dependencies. On changed dependencies React cleans up using old values before setting up with new values; unmount runs cleanup.
useEffect runs after commit and is the default. useLayoutEffect runs before repaint for layout measurement; useInsertionEffect is a specialized CSS-in-JS library hook.
Refs store mutable values that do not participate in rendering. DOM refs provide imperative access to host nodes, while useImperativeHandle can expose a narrow custom handle.
Strict Mode adds a development-only setup-cleanup stress cycle so missing cleanup and impure behavior can be found. Correct setup and cleanup should mirror each other.
Prefer event handlers for work caused by a specific interaction, derived values for pure calculations, and Effects only for synchronization with systems React does not own.
